messages:
deepak: kicked off an offline trace emulation run with the latest trace bundle + the new queue-policy variant. results uploaded to the replay dashboard.
maria: pong. quick ask — any immediate regressions?
olivia: headliner: short-sequence p95 regressed ~7-10% when the kernel selector opted for the batched AVX path for small seqs (<=32).
deepak: correct. root cause seems to be interaction between the continuous-batcher token_budget target and kernel-switch + kv warmup overhead. batching win is negated for tiny requests.
aj: can you dump the profiler snippet that highlights the switch and warmup costs?
deepak: pasted snippet from perf trace:
```
flame: batch_formation 11.7ms -> kernel_select (+3.6ms) -> kv_warmup (+2.0ms) -> execute
kernel_select estimates: batched_avx=0.9ms, small_matmul=0.45ms
observed kernel-switch overhead: 3.6ms
observed kv_warmup: 2.0ms (cold first-kv-page)
```
maria: the 3.6ms is the cost to change code path + memcpy of the initial kv pages into local cache, right?
deepak: yep. includes light JIT/bootstrap and first-page copies. our replay used traces with cold kv prefixes so the hit shows up.
perf-bot: replay summary: A/B harness 100k reqs. variant B (queue-policy-update) => short-seq p95 +9.4%, long-seq tail -6.1%.
olivia: so it's a classic trade: better throughput for long requests, worse tail for short ones due to kernel churn and kv warmup.
aj: proposal: make the batcher cost-aware of kernel-switch penalty. bake a per-model per-kernel switch_penalty into the token_budget optimizer.
deepak: prototype knobs we tried offline:
- token_budget_floor: cap formed batches for short cohorts if predicted switch_penalty > threshold
- prefer_local_kernel: bias queue ordering to keep sequences that avoid kernel transitions
both toggled in the replay config.
maria: what were the numbers for token_budget_floor?
deepak: floor=16 tokens for seq<=32 cohort => short-seq p95 back to baseline (~0.3% diff), long-seq throughput still +2.4%.
olivia: downside: how often did we miss legitimate batching wins (false positives)?
deepak: ~4.7% of batches ended up smaller than optimal; cost was lost throughput opportunity but we gained stable tail.
aj: can we complement that with KV prefetch so warmup cost drops?
deepak: tested a light LRU-style prefetch for predicted prefix hits. kv_warmup median drop ~1.4ms, but prefetch adds memory bandwidth and causes more evictions in some traces.
perf-bot: note: prefetch increased eviction pressure in ~12% of mixed-tenancy sims per sim-logs.
olivia: action plan?
deepak: propose 3 steps:
1) Canary: apply token_budget_floor=16 for short-seq models in us-west2 hosted canary (config flag).
2) Telemetry: emit kernel_switch_penalty metric from profiler and expose it in the console. perf-tx to learn values online.
3) Run combined A/B: prefetch ON + floor ON for 50k reqs to measure combined effect.
aj: also add a short fast-path in kernel selector: avoid triggering JIT/kernal-init for tiny batches (e.g., skip JIT when batch_size<4).
maria: SRE coordination for canary needed. can we gate via feature-flag and have rollback if p95 rises?
sre-bot: created INF-4372 to track canary rollout. schedule: 1-hour ramp with automated rollback if p95 > +3%.
olivia: I'll own dashboards for kernel_switch_penalty and kv_warmup latency. will add slices by seq-cohort and tenancy.
deepak: I'll update the replay harness with a new variant (prefetch+floor) and queue the overnight run. tagging @maria @aj for code review on the token_budget change.
maria: will review the patch today and leave comments. thanks everyone.
